key_insight: SAGE-Net fuses crystallographic semantics directly into geometric message passing, so textual structure descriptions can guide atom-level learning instead of being added only after encoding.
engineering_relevance: This improves property prediction and synthesizability screening for materials design workflows, helping prioritize candidate crystals more accurately and efficiently.
method: Semantic-Guided Message Passing (SGMP) injects description-derived chemistry and crystallography into GNN updates.
The framework is plug-and-play across multiple crystal-graph backbones.
It enables multimodal learning to shape local geometric interactions during encoding.
evidence_signal: Across JARVIS-DFT benchmarks, SAGE-Net achieved the lowest MAE on 8 of 10 regression targets and showed strong classification performance and high recall for synthesizability.
watch_item: Performance and interpretability depend on the quality and availability of crystal descriptions, so noisy or inconsistent semantics could limit gains in real deployment.
paper_title: SAGE-Net: Semantics-Augmented Geometric Encoder for Material Property Prediction
